Mainly reliant on rng, not that fun.
Not Recommended. 

Wasting 30min to an hour and loosing because of some OP boss that is impossible to beat with your shitty deck is fairly painfully. At a certain point in any run skill goes out the window, where all that remains is maths. It does not matter how you use your deck, if the enemy has more HP then you can deal with than nothing will remain between them and you Pyre. Without any kind of meta skills/options that can be used (e.g Potions from slay the spire, or the bonus items you can use in Transcyption), it feels like your game is already over before you even get to the final boss. 

While mentioning Slay the Spire, Monster Train 2 also has a similar issue where you need to unlock new cards/artifacts/pyres. Early run-throughs feel like a reel struggle as a new players being reliant on all the low-level / starter cards that clog your deck, causing the player to spent large amounts of currency to remove those weak cards from their deck only for the presented options that could replace them being remarkably weak without any kinds of upgrades.

A true sequel that takes, builds, and improve upon the original. Core gameplay remains near identical to the first Monster Train, but the improvements such as the Deployment Phase and Pyre Hearts offers more substances to Monster Train 2.

The first Monster Train was quite the trip through the rings of Hell, but Monster Train 2 expands it to the Heavens themselves, figuratively and literally.
I absolutely loved Monster Train 1, and this is the best sequel I could have asked for! THANK YOU!

Best rogue-like deck builder since Slay the Spire. The sheer magnitude of potential deck combinations that exist in this game are absurd. While there are some fundamentally OP deck combos for each "hero", the game provides a good balance of rock/paper/scissors to keep you from sticking to the same strategy. 

If you value your free-time, consider not purchasing this game.

More of the same but imo better. Improving in the mechanics and lessons learned from 1. The new clans are a great to play with their unique mechanics. The addition in equipment and rooms are welcome. Overall it feels more balanced and streamlined.

I was a bit unsure on the first play through thinking 1 was better. It did not take me many runs to realize how wrong I was. This game is on the level of Balatro in greatness. The amount of variation from the selecting different races means the replayability is insane.

A must get for anyone that enjoys deckbuilding roguelites.

If you liked the 1st game, definitely get this.

For some reason, I like this one more than the 1st game.
It seems like things mesh better (though you can still get brutalized on occasion). I really like the Fungoid clan, but all of them seem to work together once you unlock their alternate hero versions (also allows you to change what cards you get for using them as a secondary clan)

I also feel like most of the unlocks are less grindy, more approachable goals.

I find myself wanting to do more runs without feeling like taking a break and playing something different.

I just reached the secret, and wow. That definitely puts this over the top.

I don't often write reviews for games, but Ive had so much fun with this game that I felt like I had to write one. There is so much variability, even after hundreds of hours of playing most runs feel different from each other, and all the clans/bosses are really unique! 10/10 keep up the great work!

+ More Monster Train!
+ Interesting card combo's

- Did not like most "races". Felt weird or complex
- Runs took me too long (Can speed it up but than I can't really see whats going on)
- Kicked ass only to get destroyed by some bosses

My enjoyment:
5/10 Slay the spire kept met hooked, this one does not

I like it, but I can't give it a 5 out of 5.

On the one hand, the new additions are great. This isn't just a copy of the first game only with different monsters and abilities. They added a lot! Being able to unlock and use different pyres, equipment and room cards, dimensional challenges and more.

However, as far as the the design and UI go, I'm not a fan. You've got these hexagonal metal and rivet buttons and other elements, along with a rock/metal soundtrack, all of which fits the "hell" theme. But then you have these pastel colored, "cute" monsters, much more "feminine" in their designs. These things sort of clash and don't make for a coherent design throughout the game. I especially dislike the little hymnist punk birds with their instruments. They feel really out of place. It feels like they let each person do tehir own thing, and then meshed it all together.

Nevertheless, I still enjoy the game and recommend it!

If you loved the first one, you will love the new one. If you didn't like the first one, you can skip this one. But 95% of players liked it so you probably will like it
In general, its more of the same, with some new effects and added features/unlockables that improve upon the same game, but it is relatively the same gameplay wise.
If you are new to the game, its a pretty "simple" but very strategic kind of deck building game, where not only it matters which cards you play but in which orders your units are placed. There is a lot of variety based on enemy effects, some will atack all your units stopping you from having a glass cannon, others will make it so that you get poisoned after you kill them

Same amazing formula as the first Monster Train, then times 2 literally. If you liked the first, you will be extremely happy, and if you like any other rogue like deck builder, this game is a must. Do note though, it progressively gets MUCH better, so power through the start of the game.

A textbook example of Take The First Game And Make It Better. More complexity, more difficulty but in a good way, more game modes, more story (made more explicit), music goes a little harder, everything is just more and better.

You do not need to have played MT1 to play MT2, but you might find the story more satisfying if you have, and of course you would have a leg up on mechanics that return from the first game. MT1 is also pretty cheap during any of the usual sales.

My only complaint is that I don't understand how to unlock all the story scenes. I just stopped getting new ones after a while and my friend kept getting more and we can't figure out what we're doing differently.

Monster Train keeps giving and giving. If you like Slay the spire, you are gonna love this well made sequel to the 1st Monster Train. Awesome feeling of accomplishment when discovering a new broken comp you had no idea existed.
It's been a long time since I've played a sequel that improves on the first game in every single way.
More variety and less randomness than a slay the spire, and the music is already saved in my fav in spotify.

Everything you loved about Monster Train, but even better. Devs are quick to tweak and add QoL. If you loved MT1, you'll love it. If you didn't, you probably won't. If you haven't played the first one, it's probably cheaper, but I think this one is a better game in almost every way.
I have over 1000 hours into Monster Train. Monster Train 2 is simply better in every way. Fantastic game!

Don't waste your money on this game. The original Monster Train is much better. This one is way too hard, with super overpowered bosses. Devs need to tone it down quite a bit to make it at least enjoyable. I will be uninstalling this game.

Better graphics. Better balancing. Better save/reversion management. More interesting events with interesting decisions.

My short list of complaints is that there's a mediocre story now, and the music might be 10% worse than the original.

I am short of words. It is a marvel all round.Kudos to the devs for optimising so even intel uhd potato pcs like me can play it

Some clans are harder than others, but overall the mechanics and synergies are great.

If you liked the first game, don't think long - take MT2 just right now. All the clans from the original game are included btw.

The only thing Monster Train is 100% better than Monster Train 2 is soundtrack, IMHO.
competent game, don't like the plot but it can be skipped, don't like the art style but don't hate it enough to not play the game, like the combination of clans, like the playstyle choices
Top-tier deckbuilder. Extremely replayable due to the variety of ways to form decks and modify runs. I am still discovering new events and ways to play better after 150 hours.

If you like Slay the Spire then this is your type of game. The animation style is bright and lively and the little side stories give a bit more character to each of the generals and even troops. This game keeps what made the original game so much fun and gives just a little bit more. The new factions are somewhat comparable to the originals so the tactics and playstyle translate well without being direct copies of one another. 

Overall great game

It has 5 new clans, 10 new heroes, as well as the original clans and heroes; the number of different playstyles and strategies is insane! Once I loaded the game up for the first time I couldn't stop playing. This game is worth every penny, and is only going to get better with the content updates.

Have been fortunate enough to be an official playtester for this absolute gem of a game, the amount of blood sweat and tears the devs poured (and still keep pouring) into this game to make it the best it can be is absolutely amazing.

THIS is how you do a sequel. Take the beloved original, tweak some of the features that needed tweaking, then add in a bunch of new mechanics that can cause utter chaos and destruction every run. 

More of a focus on utilizing units and all floors instead of solo carrying on one floor, which I think adds so much more strategy to the game. Equipment for your units and floor upgrades come into play, so taking draw as your boss reward isn't the instant pick anymore. Space and energy have a lot more weight to runs. 

Long and short of this, if you liked MT1, this is a must buy. Excuse me while I continue to sink 1k hours into this...

As someone with 68 hours in Monster Train 1, I am excited that Monster Train 2 improves a lot on an already exciting game. In Monster Train 1, you could only go up in Covenant (difficulty) ranks (like the Slay the Spire ascension levels) and try out different deck combinations as you replayed the game. In 2, you can now follow a story line as you go up in covenant ranks as well as try out the 22 different dimensional challenges.

Even though I know the game well, I have only won 2 out of my first 10 or so runs, so the game is still appropriately difficult while giving more you more choice, such as which Pyre Heart to run each game. I can tell that the numbers that both friendly and enemy units do have been pumped up, which i think is fun given the addition of equipment and room cards that can be put on units to make them even stronger.

I'm already looking forward to the upcoming collabs with Balatro and Cult of the Lamb, but the base game is very good and a marked improvement on the first game!

I totally loved Monster Train 1, but this beats it in every possible way. I have played for 28 hours now, and I feel that I've just scratched the surface. So many challenges, unlocks, crazy synergies, records to beat, run modifiers... I love it all. And even more is coming in the promised free updates? Amazing, money well spent. Recommended!

An absolutely phenomenal follow up to the first game. New fresh content; familiar faces and trinkets for the first game. The developers really knocked it out of the park; this game is worth every penny.

Oh dang, I've only owned this game for less than a day and I've already played almost 10 hours...

This sequel has new sets of cards, new abilities, new mechanics that shake up what the first game was-- while still maintaining the Monster Train's identity, and all the things I LOVE about the first game. And now, you can also unlock new PYRES for your train with different abilities! Lots of little customizations, mutators, and even bits of lore that you discover by playing the game.

It's a love letter to its own prequel. The first Monster Train is my favorite roguelike card game, and it feels like this sequel will be another joyful timesink for me.

10/10
Incredible game - loved the first one, and the second is no exception. If you love card-battlers/rogue-likes, you have to play this game.

Best Roguelike out there in my opinion. So many classes, builds, combinations and so much replayability and such a great OST on top of it.

Give it a try if this genre is for you, you won't be disappointed.

I like it a lot, I think overall it's an improvement over MT1. way more balanced and less RNG dependent. you're not gonna lose a run because you don't draw your vital cards on turn 1 or 2. my only real complaint is the bizarre decision to reduce covenant levels from 25 to 10. they wanted people to not feel like they're grinding endlessly to get to higher levels but also that's the whole point of a roguelike game. I'll probably end up playing this one way less because of that because there's just less to do.

You'll mess with this. The first one is a great game as well but you don't need to play the first one to play this and if you can only buy one, buy this one.
really addictive. once you understand what's going on, you just can't stop. there's so many combinations that can yield the most astonishing synergies. highly recommend.
